title: Young's Double Slit Experiment: Fringe Width

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Wave Optics

explanation: Fringe width (distance between two consecutive bright or two consecutive dark fringes) in Young's double slit experiment depends directly on wavelength λ and screen distance D, and inversely on slit separation d. This means: using longer-wavelength light, moving the screen farther away, or bringing the slits closer together all INCREASE fringe width (fringes more spread out and easier to observe).
commonMistakes: Forgetting to convert wavelength (usually given in nm) into metres before substituting — a very common unit-conversion slip.

Assuming fringe width is the same for all colours of light in white-light interference — different wavelengths (colours) give different fringe widths, causing coloured fringes except at the central maximum.
genZNote: Bigger screen distance, wider fringes — Young's double slit rewards a little extra distance.
